subject: chemistry-9
description: Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes), unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkenes and alkynes), combustion, substitution and addition reactions, physical properties, and uses of methane, ethene, and ethyne.

questions.question: Which of the following is the general formula of alkanes?
questions.explanation: Alkanes follow the formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂

questions.question: Alkanes are called saturated hydrocarbons because they:
questions.explanation: Saturation means only single covalent bonds

questions.question: The classification of hydrocarbons mainly depends on which characteristic of carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: Hydrocarbons are grouped based on whether carbon atoms share single, double, or triple bonds

questions.question: Why is methane considered the first member of the alkane series?
questions.explanation: Methane has the minimum possible carbon atoms required to form an alkane molecule

questions.question: In alkane molecules, how many covalent bonds does each carbon atom form?
questions.explanation: Carbon completes its octet by forming four covalent bonds in stable organic compounds

questions.question: The addition of hydrogen across a carbon–carbon multiple bond is chemically termed as which process?
questions.explanation: Hydrogenation involves the addition of hydrogen atoms across double or triple bonds

questions.question: When an alkyne undergoes complete hydrogenation, how many hydrogen molecules are added?
questions.explanation: An alkyne has a triple bond and requires two hydrogen molecules for full saturation

questions.question: The first product formed when ethyne undergoes hydrogenation under controlled conditions is which compound?
questions.explanation: Partial hydrogenation of ethyne converts the triple bond into a double bond first

questions.question: Reduction of alkyl halides to alkanes requires the presence of which metal?
questions.explanation: Zinc reacts with aqueous acid to generate nascent hydrogen for reduction

questions.question: Which reagent is commonly used along with zinc for reducing alkyl halides?
questions.explanation: Aqueous acids provide hydrogen ions that help generate nascent hydrogen

questions.question: Which method directly converts unsaturated hydrocarbons into saturated hydrocarbons?
questions.explanation: Hydrogenation removes unsaturation by adding hydrogen across multiple bonds

questions.question: Addition of nascent hydrogen to an alkyl halide is classifie under which reaction type?
questions.explanation: Gain of hydrogen by a compound is defined as a reduction reaction

questions.question: Alkanes do not dissolve in water primarily because of which reason?
questions.explanation: Non-polar alkanes cannot interact effectively with polar water molecules

questions.question: Alkanes containing up to four carbon atoms usually exist in which physical state at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Short-chain alkanes have weak intermolecular forces, so they remain gaseous

questions.question: A chemical reaction that occurs in the presence of sunlight is known as what type of reaction?
questions.explanation: Light-initiated reactions are classified as photochemical reactions

questions.question: The reaction between an alkane and a halogen is classified as which reaction type?
questions.explanation: A halogen atom replaces a hydrogen atom during alkane halogenation

questions.question: What is the main organic product when methane reacts with chlorine in diffused sunlight?
questions.explanation: Controlled halogenation substitutes one hydrogen atom with chlorine

questions.question: Complete combustion of alkanes produces which main products?
questions.explanation: Adequate oxygen ensures full oxidation to carbon dioxide and water

questions.question: Why are lighter alkanes preferred as domestic and industrial fuels?
questions.explanation: Lighter gaseous alkanes burn cleanly with controlled combustion and release large amounts of heat energy per gram.

questions.question: Incomplete combustion of methane occurs mainly due to which condition?
questions.explanation: Insufficient oxygen prevents full oxidation of carbon atoms

questions.question: Which substances may form during the incomplete combustion of methane?
questions.explanation: Partial oxidation forms toxic CO and soot particles

questions.question: The presence of carbon particles during combustion indicates which type of reaction?
questions.explanation: Solid carbon formation shows a lack of sufficient oxygen for complete burning
